title: Nonlinear Spin Polarization Enables Néel Order Switching in Centrosymmetric Altermagnets
authors: Sunit Das, Sayan Sarkar, Amit Agarwal
abstract: Deterministic electrical switching of the Néel order remains challenging in centrosymmetric altermagnets, where linear current-induced spin polarization is forbidden by inversion symmetry. Here, we establish a nonlinear route to Néel order control. Spin group symmetry shows that, in the nonrelativistic limit, the nonlinear spin polarization is constrained along the Néel vector, with a staggered response allowed in $8$ of the $10$ nontrivial spin-Laue groups. Although this Néel spin polarization is torque-inactive by itself, finite spin-orbit coupling can generate an additional uniform component transverse to the Néel vector. Using a minimal model for the $d$-wave altermagnet FeSb$_2$, we demonstrate the coexistence of the nonrelativistic staggered response with an SOC-induced uniform transverse component. Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation-based macro-spin simulations reveal that the transverse component alone produces oscillatory dynamics, whereas its cooperative action with the staggered response enables deterministic $180^\circ$ reversal. We further show that changing the electric field orientation reverses the staggered spin response and selects the switching direction, while the opposite Néel states can be distinguished by their anomalous Hall response. Our results establish a nonlinear electrical write-read scheme for centrosymmetric altermagnets.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to electrically switch the Néel order in centrosymmetric altermagnets, overcoming the symmetry-imposed prohibition on linear current effects. By analyzing nonlinear spin polarization, the authors show that the combination of a staggered response and a SOC-induced transverse component generates the necessary torque for deterministic switching. This establishes a novel nonlinear write-read mechanism for these materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving deterministic electrical switching of the Néel order in centrosymmetric altermagnets, a process hindered because linear current-induced spin polarization is forbidden by inversion symmetry.
main_result: The authors establish a nonlinear electrical write-read scheme by showing that the interplay between the nonrelativistic staggered spin response and a SOC-induced uniform transverse component enables deterministic $180^\circ$ reversal of the Néel order.
method: The study combines symmetry analysis using spin group theory to constrain nonlinear spin polarization, quantum kinetic calculations (density matrix evolution), and macro-spin simulations using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
model_or_system: The research focuses on centrosymmetric altermagnets, using a minimal tight-binding model for $	ext{FeSb}_2$ as a concrete example. The physics is governed by the interplay between nonrelativistic spin-split bands and finite spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
key_observables: Néel vector reversal ($180^\circ$ switching), anomalous Hall response (for state readout), and the coexistence/interaction of uniform and staggered nonlinear spin polarization components.
important_parameters: The mechanism is critically dependent on the presence of finite SOC, which generates the necessary transverse component, and the electric field orientation, which controls the switching direction.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a perturbative expansion in the weak-field regime and assumes the validity of the minimal model for the altermagnet $	ext{FeSb}_2$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the mechanism: the nonrelativistic limit yields a torque-inactive, collinear response, while finite SOC introduces a transverse component, leading to a non-zero torque capable of driving reversal.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the symmetry constraints on nonlinear spin polarization in the nonrelativistic limit. It then incorporates finite SOC to generate a transverse component. Finally, macro-spin simulations demonstrate how the cooperation between the staggered and transverse components enables deterministic switching, forming a write-read scheme.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter magnetism, the concept of using non-linear, symmetry-protected responses (like the second-order polarization) to control quantum states (magnetic order) is highly relevant to open quantum systems and non-equilibrium dynamics.

(a) In the nonrelativistic limit, centrosymmetric altermagnets can host a staggered nonlinear spin polarization collinear with the N´eel vector, δSA = −δSB. Being parallel to the local moments, this response is torque-inactive. (b) Finite SOC generates an additional transverse spin component, so that the total sublattice spin polarizations are no longer exactly opposite, δSA ̸= −δSB. The resulting coexistence of transverse and staggered collinear spin polarization components produces the torques required for electrical reversal of the N´eel order.

(a) Schematic device configurations for deterministic switching between the two opposite N´eel states, achieved by changing the orientation of the applied electric field.
